title: Noor & Julian
description: Julian, a French software engineer living in Amsterdam, met Noor Van Dijk 8 months ago at a networking event. Brilliant and engaging, she won his heart and then convinced him to invest 15 000

questions.question: Thomas told me that the NGO Stichting Groen doesn't really exist. Check how long the website has been up.
questions.hint: Take a look at the open tabs in the Safari browser. Noor visited the NGO's website; scroll all the way down to the bottom of the homepage to find the legal notice and the year the site was launched.

questions.question: 7 months… And how long has Noor been working there?
questions.hint: Open LinkedIn and go to Noor's profile — her experience section shows exactly when she started this position.

questions.question: She joined the NGO one month before the website was created… Who is the founder of Stichting Groen?
questions.hint: Stay on LinkedIn and find the official company page for Stichting Groen. Their profile information clearly states the identity of its creator.

questions.question: Farid… Find me his full name please
questions.hint: Open Contacts and search for Farid — his profile gives his full last name.

questions.question: Farid Nkosi… Noor sent him something about me, if so tell me what they talked about.
questions.hint: Open Gmail and search for messages linked to Farid. Open the email in Noor's sent folder: the subject line perfectly sums up their conversation.

questions.question: She sent him my bank details for the wire transfer… How much did I transfer again?
questions.hint: Open Revolut and look in the transaction history for the money received from Julian — the exact amount appears by clicking on the transfer line.

questions.question: 15,000€… They're planning to ask me for more money? Find out and tell me how much.
questions.hint: Open WhatsApp and go to the conversation with Farid to find the total amount he wants to reach. Then subtract what Julian has already paid to find out how much more they're going to ask him for.

questions.question: 25,000€ more, what a bunch of scammers… Am I the only victim, or tell me the first and last name of the other person.
questions.hint: Scroll further up in the conversation with Farid — about 3 weeks ago, they talk about another person and a transfer.

questions.question: So there's another victim… And how much has Noor collected in total?
questions.hint: Look in the Notes app for a locked note — the code is based on Noor's date of birth, which you'll find in her contact profile.

questions.question: 23,000€… Not bad for someone who supposedly had nothing. Still need to find out where she comes from. Where did she work before setting all this up?
questions.hint: Go to the Gmail app, open the side menu and go to the Trash. You'll find an official contract termination letter there that mentions the name of her former firm.

questions.question: She left everything behind to set up this scam… Where did she plan to go if someone starts digging?
questions.hint: Look at the most recent messages in the WhatsApp conversation with Farid. Noor explicitly mentions the name of the place abroad where she plans to flee if things go wrong.

questions.question: She's going to Bali… When exactly is the ticket for?
questions.hint: First find the ticket reference received in Gmail. Then open the Notes app and look for the note called Codes: find this reference in the middle of the list to read the number of days remaining before departure.

questions.question: They're flying off soon... But wait, chances are Farid isn't going with her to Bali to throw us off the trail. Find the exact destination of his own flight!
questions.hint: Someone modified Farid's ticket to make it look like he was going to Bali. Open Noor's Drive app, open Farid's ticket document, then tap the Version History icon in the top right corner: the version from June 17 reveals the real destination.

questions.question: Cairo?! They're splitting up so I can't follow them both... I bet they bought burner phones to stay in touch over there. Find the exact model of the device she secretly got her hands on!
questions.hint: To find out the model of the hidden phone, log into Noor's Amazon account using the email address from her Gmail app. Decode the memo at the bottom of the locked note Overzicht: it asks you to combine the first name of the NGO's founder with the year of their very first architecture position visible on LinkedIn. Once logged in, look for the order that matches the locker code from her Departure note.

questions.question: A Nokia 105... She must have already set up Farid's new burner SIM card so they can call each other abroad. Find the full phone number of this secret line!
questions.hint: Farid explains in WhatsApp that his secret number starts with the country code +20 followed by the digits on his SIM card. Open the Photo Gallery app to locate the image of the SIM card he sent her and read the 9 digits printed below the barcode.

textSuccess: Damn… Thank you. Thank you for everything. I can't believe it. 15 000€, a fake NGO, an accomplice, another victim… and her planning her escape to Bali while Farid heads to Cairo. Everything was calculated from the start. From the very first evening at the networking event. I'm calling the police now. With everything we found — the wire transfers, the messages with Farid, the locked note, the plane tickets — they won't be able to deny it. Thank you for digging into this. Without you, I would have lost 25 000€ more.

onboardingContent.text: Hey... My name is Julian. A mutual friend told me you could help me. I'm an engineer, I'm not used to this kind of situation at all, but I'm completely lost right now and I need someone.

I've been with Noor for 8 months. We met in Amsterdam, I fell for her right away. She convinced me to invest €15,000 in her reforestation NGO... and this morning my friend Thomas called me from Paris to tell me the NGO doesn't really exist.

For the past 3 weeks Noor has been more and more distant, she dodges my questions. This morning she left and forgot her phone on the table. I don't know if she forgot it or if she ran away. But I need to know the truth about her.

I have her phone in my hands. I can't do this alone, I'm too emotionally involved. You can look at this with a fresh perspective. Go through her messages, her apps, her contacts... Tell me what you find.

notes.title: Recipe — Quick shakshuka
notes.content:
Ingredients (serves 2):
- 1 can of crushed tomatoes
- 1 red bell pepper
- 1 onion
- 2 garlic cloves
- 4 eggs
- Cumin, smoked paprika, harissa
- Feta + fresh coriander

Method: sauté onion + garlic + pepper. Add tomatoes + spices. Let reduce for 10 min. Make wells, crack the eggs into them. Cover for 5-7 min. Serve with pita bread.

→ Delicious and quick. Mum would approve.

An increasing number of Dutch firms are embracing reclaimed materials. The *Cradle to Cradle* movement is gaining ground in public tenders.

Amsterdam is experimenting with mass timber micro-neighborhoods to address the housing crisis without disrupting the existing urban fabric.

# Stichting Groen
### 🌱 Planting Today for Tomorrow

![dutch forest](https://imgcaller.3t.net.vn/MobileDetective/v1/_external/images.unsplash.com/photo-1448375240586-882707db888b_b6c0720e.jpg)

> *Together, we are reforesting the Netherlands. Every tree planted is an act for future generations.*

---

## Our Mission

Stichting Groen is a non-profit organization founded to combat deforestation and promote biodiversity in the Netherlands. We work in partnership with municipalities, farmers and volunteers to replant native forests on degraded land.

---

## Our Ongoing Projects

### 🌳 Project Veluwe Vert
Reforestation of 120 hectares in the Veluwe region, in collaboration with Staatsbosbeheer. Species planted: pedunculate oak, European beech, downy birch.

**Progress:** 68% · **Trees planted:** 84,000 / 125,000

---

### 🌿 Living Hedgerows — Groningen
Restoring ecological corridors between agricultural plots in the province of Groningen. Program co-funded by the Province and the European Union (LIFE fund).

**Progress:** 41% · **Km of hedgerows:** 23 / 56

---

### 🏙️ Urban Forests — Amsterdam & Utrecht
Planting micro-forests using the Miyawaki method in neighborhoods with low green coverage. 14 active sites in 2024.

**Progress:** 55% · **Sites completed:** 8 / 14

---

## Support Us

Your donation directly funds the purchase of seedlings, volunteer training and the scientific monitoring of our plantings.

| Amount | Impact |
|---|---|
| 10 EUR | 3 trees planted |
| 25 EUR | 8 trees + 1 year monitoring |
| 50 EUR | Sponsorship of an ecological corridor |
| 100 EUR | Stichting Groen Patron |

messages.content: Hi Noor, I'm reaching out further to your presentation at the "Green Transition and NGO Governance" webinar organized by Impact Hub Amsterdam a few weeks ago. Your approach to impact measurement in non-profit organizations was particularly relevant. I'm currently working on a European programme that could benefit from your expertise. Would you be open to having a conversation?

Hi Olivier, thank you so much for your feedback on that presentation, it's very encouraging. I'm of course open to a conversation. Could you tell me a bit more about the European programme you're referring to? That would help me assess how I might be able to contribute in a meaningful way.

Of course. It's a Horizon Europe programme aimed at developing standardized indicators to assess the environmental impact of NGOs operating across several member states. We're looking for independent consultants to co-develop the methodological framework with our teams in Brussels. The project would kick off in September 2026 for a duration of eighteen months. Does that align with your availability?

This is a project I'm genuinely interested in — the standardization of impact indicators is something I've worked extensively on over the past few years. As for September, my availability will depend on how a current assignment progresses, but in principle it should be doable. I'd suggest a 30-minute call during the week of August 4 to discuss it in more concrete terms — what do you think?
Perfect — would Tuesday, August 5 at 10am work for you? I'll send you the video conference link upon confirmation.
Tuesday, August 5 at 10am works perfectly for me. Talk soon, Olivier, and thanks again for this opportunity.

linkedinConversations.participantHeadline: Chargée de mission Environnement at Gemeente Amsterdam

messages.content: Hey Noor! I just saw that you published an article on LinkedIn about B Corp certification for small non-profit organizations. Really interesting! I'd love to get your take on something: do you think this kind of certification is realistic for a municipal or semi-public organization? It's something we've been debating internally lately.

Hey Charlotte! Good question. Honestly, B Corp in a semi-public context is tricky — the assessment process is designed for private entities and some criteria (governance, ownership structure) simply don't apply. That said, the approach itself — even without the final certification — can be an excellent internal diagnostic tool. You could use it as a reference framework without necessarily aiming for the official label. What's driving this conversation internally?

That's exactly what I thought, but I was struggling to argue it in front of management. You just gave me the words I was missing! It's actually an initiative pushed by a new director who comes from the private sector and wants to "showcase our CSR commitments." Using the framework as a reference without going for the label is a really interesting angle. Would you be available for an informal chat about it? Even a twenty-minute call would be enough.

Happy to! I totally get the dynamic you're describing — it's a classic when someone comes in from the private sector. Send me a few time slots and we'll find a moment. I could also share some resources on similar cases in Belgium and Denmark that went through a comparable process.
Great, I'll send those over first thing tomorrow morning. And yes, the Belgian and Danish examples would be really useful — thanks in advance! Talk soon.
